Sabine Hossenfelder
Sabine Hossenfelder
Sabine Hossenfelder ( born 18 September 1976 ) is a German author and theoretical physicist who researches quantum gravity . Sabine Hossenfelder is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where Sabine Hossenfelder leads the Superfluid Dark Matter group . Sabine Hossenfelder is the author of Lost in Math : How Beauty Leads Physics Astray , which explores the concept of elegance in fundamental physics and cosmology . Education . Sabine Hossenfelder completed Sabine Hossenfelder's undergraduate degree in 1997 at Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität in Frankfurt am Main . Sabine Hossenfelder remained there for a Masters degree , and Sabine Hossenfelder wrote a thesis under the supervision of Walter Greiner titled Particle Production in Time Dependent Gravitational Fields , which Sabine Hossenfelder completed in 2000 . Sabine Hossenfelder received Sabine Hossenfelder's doctorate from Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität in Frankfurt am Main in 2003 , for the thesis Black Holes in Large Extra Dimensions under the supervision of Horst Stöcker . Research . Sabine Hossenfelder remained in Germany until 2004 as a postdoctoral researcher at the GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research in Darmstadt , Germany . Sabine Hossenfelder moved to North America and completed research fellowships at the University of Arizona , Tucson , University of California , Santa Barbara and Perimeter Institute , Canada . Sabine Hossenfelder joined Nordita Institute for Theoretical Physics , Sweden , in 2009 as an Assistant Professor . In 2018 Sabine Hossenfelder was a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the Superfluid Dark Matter group . Sabine Hossenfelder research interest is in the phenomenology of quantum gravity . Sabine Hossenfelder focuses on the role of Lorentz invariance and locality , which would be altered in the discovery of quantum gravity . Sabine Hossenfelder is trying to find experimental evidence of quantum gravity . Since 2007 Sabine Hossenfelder has been involved with the annual conference series Experimental Search for Quantum Gravity . Sabine Hossenfelder has created a number of YouTube videos exploring quantum gravity . Sabine Hossenfelder has been employed by the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the Superfluid Dark Matter group since 2015 , where Sabine Hossenfelder leads the Analog Systems for Gravity Duals group . Another area of Sabine Hossenfelder's research are foundations of quantum mechanics , where Sabine Hossenfelder has argued against free will and in favor of superdeterminism . Sabine Hossenfelder has also been researching since at least 2008 on how technology is changing researchers ability to publicize , discuss , or publish researchers's research , when Sabine Hossenfelder co-organized the Science in the 21st Century workshop . Public engagement and scientific achievements .

Sabine Hossenfelder has also been researching since at least 2008 on how technology is changing researchers ability to publicize , discuss , or publish researchers's research , when Sabine Hossenfelder co-organized the Science in the 21st Century workshop . Public engagement and scientific achievements . Sabine Hossenfelder is a freelance popular science writer who has kept a blog since 2006 . Sabine Hossenfelder contributes to the Forbes column Starts with a Bang as well as Quanta Magazine , New Scientist , Nature Physics , Scientific American , Nautilus Quarterly and Physics Today . To show some gaps in the argument of Verlindes claim that gravity is an entropic force , Sabine Hossenfelder derived Verlindes formula for Newtons law of universal gravitation using a new form of an entropic variation formula that reduces to Bekenstein-Hawking entropy at the black hole event horizon . In 2016 , Sabine Hossenfelder offered to act as a physics consultant on Sabine Hossenfelder's blog—US$50 for twenty minutes of discussion—and had to recruit five extra physicists to deal with the demand . In 2017 Sabine Hossenfelder created cards featuring pioneering quantum physicists . Live Science and The Guardian quoted Sabine Hossenfelder as an authority when trying to evaluate the importance of Stephen Hawkings last scientific publication . Basic Books are the publishers of Sabine Hossenfelder first book , Lost in Math : How Beauty Leads Physics Astray , released in June 2018 . A review in Nature described Hossenfelders first book , Lost in Math : How Beauty Leads Physics Astray , released in June 2018 as provocative , and Frank Wilczek recommended Hossenfelders first book , Lost in Math : How Beauty Leads Physics Astray , released in June 2018 as an intensely personal and intellectually hard-edged book , even though Frank Wilczek disagreed with Hossenfelders first book , Lost in Math : How Beauty Leads Physics Astray , released in June 2018 on many points . Sabine Hossenfelder's 2018 book , Lost in Math , was also published in German with the title , Das hässliche Universum ( The Ugly Universe ) . Sabine Hossenfelder posits that the universe ( and the universe's particle model ) is messy , and that the universe cannot be described by a mathematical ( beautiful ) Great Unified Theory . Sabine Hossenfelder currently has an eponymously-named YouTube channel ( subtitled Science without the gobbledygook ) .
